_doc: Managed-authentication runs for the harness's `managed` direction (harness/managed.py, PROTOCOL.md § managed).
Each case is one sandboxed program: store file, environment, scripted UI answers, scripted auth-server replies
(consumed in order; an exhausted script answers every further request with a refused connection), and public
operations. `expect` holds the normalized outcome: one entry per step, the ordered trace, the store afterwards.

Secrets carry the marker in `sentinel`; the harness fails any case where it reaches a public outcome, prompt or notice. It is expected in the private channels (auth request bodies and headers, the store, a request_auth credential) — and therefore not the corpus-wide AUTH-5 sentinel, which may never appear in an expectation.
Expectations were captured from lm15-python and reviewed against AUTH-12–26 before they were pinned; a port that
disagrees is wrong unless a changes/ entry says the reference was.

cases.about: An entry without a slot record is generation 1, id legacy-xai; read-only operations never rewrite the file.
Renewing a legacy entry writes its slot record on that first managed commit.
A saved slot whose credential is due renews on request.
AUTH-20.4/20.6: a renewal marker still present once the lock is held means the renewing process died mid-exchange: indeterminate, never a second exchange of a possibly rotated token.
Replacing names the current id; the new connection is generation 2 and the old id is remembered.

cases.about: An occupied slot is connection_exists; a stale replace id is connection_changed; neither contacts anything.
R3: logout keeps a marker; the environment key is not used afterwards, across restarts.
AUTH-19: logout by a replaced id never removes the newer connection.
An env recipe stores the variable's name, never its value; the value is read at request time.
An env recipe whose variable is unset is login_required at request time, not a fallback.
A keyless local server records its URL.
A cloud recipe names an identity (AUTH-15); no credential is captured; an unknown name is refused.
A recipe with a missing required field is interaction_required before anything is written.
AUTH-25: an unreadable store is storage_unavailable, never empty, never overwritten; login stops before any network.
An unknown store version is unsupported_store_version.
AUTH-25: duplicate member names are refused before they collapse.
A provider entry that is not an object is storage_unavailable.
AUTH-20.1/R4: a bound selection follows renewals only; replacement is connection_changed, logout login_required.
AUTH-13.5: an unverified method runs only on explicit opt-in; refusal touches nothing.
Claude's hosted return page: PKCE S256, independent state, code#state pasted, JSON exchange.
AUTH-18: a pasted return from another attempt is rejected without ending the wait; nothing is exchanged until a valid one arrives.
Claude's profile does not accept a bare code without its state: rejected, asked again; here the person then gives up.
A rejected code exchange is login_denied and never retried.
The person cancels at the paste prompt: a native cancellation, the reservation released.
AUTH-13.6: with more than one selectable method the UI is asked; the answer must be an offered id.
ChatGPT device authorization: user code, polling (403 is pending), then the code+verifier exchange.
GitHub device flow, the Copilot token exchange (the API host comes from the token and is validated), then a re-mint when due.
AUTH-20.9: a proxy host outside GitHub's domains is never used as a base URL.
Kimi Code device login (JSON replies) and a rate-limited renewal that keeps the credential.
Meta device login, then a key mint; renewal is a re-mint; a 401 from the mint is permanent.
AUTH-7 under a managed Auth: explicit entry, the saved connection, env keys shown and not consulted.
